issue.title: Define Translation Agent Skills for Airflow Terminology
issue.body:
## Why

With recent agentic evolution, integrating LLM CLIs (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.) with rendering prompts, such as in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/55917 for automating translations **can be replaced by [“Agent Skills”](https://agentskills.io) as a more generic, up-to-date, and lower-maintenance solution**.

## How

Add Airflow terminology–specific translation skills under `.github/skills/translation`.

- For `SKILL.md`, we should only mention **global-level** Airflow terminology guidelines.
  - e.g., use `Dag` instead of `DAG`; some Airflow terms should remain in English, such as `Dag` and `XCom`.

- Each `locales/{locale-name}.md` file should document locale-specific guidelines, based on the existing locale files under `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/{locale-name}/`.

```bash
.github/skills/airflow-translations
├── locales
│   ├── ar.md
│   # ... all the locales we currently have, each with locale-specific skills
│   └── zh-TW.md
└── SKILL.md # global-level Airflow terminology guidelines
```

If your locale does not yet have ‎`airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/{locale-name}/README.md`:

- Please describe why we selected specific terms for the local translation in that file.

## Sub-issues

- Global-level agent skills
- Locale-specific agent skills

### Committer

- [x] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.

comments.body:
Hi @jason810496 ,

I created this draft PR (https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/62059) after doing some exploration. I think we don't have a `SKILL.md`, or a sample locale-specific instruction, defined yet. So, I would like to open this draft to ensure I am on the right direction. If I am on the right direction, I can experiment with these skill instructions, and we can probably iterate on it. It would be great if eventually these two files can be used as a reference to implement other locale-specific instruction.

Basically, in `SKILL.md`, we could provide a high-level instruction to guide the agent on the following:
1. where to find locale-specific guidelines
2. general rules across locales
3. step-by-step workflow
4. Airflow terminologies / conventions

locale-specific instruction includes specific rules for translating from English to the specific language. Also, as mentioned in dev list,  the reasons for its terminology choices.

I wonder if we already have such standard or what we should include in the skill instruction. If not, probably it is a good time to discuss on this aspect, and this could help standardize other implementations.

I also found an issue related to licensing when creating the `SKILL.md`. As the YAML formatter must be on the first line of the file, the agent skill specification provides a key "license". However, the pre-commit hook will attempt to add license, and TOC, etc. to the skill instruction, which could break the skill parsing. I am not sure what would be the best way to handle the licensing, and would appreciate any feedback on it.

Thanks,

> It would be great if eventually these two files can be used as a reference to implement other locale-specific instruction.

Your draft PR for adding `SKILL.md` and zh-CN locale instruction is already good enough to merge as references from my perspective.

> I wonder if we already have such standard or what we should include in the skill instruction. If not, probably it is a good time to discuss on this aspect, and this could help standardize other implementations.

We don’t have standard yet, but I think we just need to iterate on the Global SKILL.md to align the generic rules.

For rest of the locale.md, they will be more flexible and not that strict.  As long as the maintainers of that language agree with the locale.md, it should be fine.


The last licensing issue, I think specifying the key in metadata header _should_ be enough, but I will raise awareness in dev mailing list to make sure we follow the ASF guidelines.
I just noticed the commit: https://github.com/apache/airflow/commit/e8c261fb6065dbf3b9659c4a9ec55338b6c7b806, should we refine the merged `SKILL.md` and `zh-CN.md` to incorporate the changes?

Yes, I think we should follow the new convention, thanks!
